name: EuroSAT
description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images covering 13 spectral bands and consisting of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images for land use and land cover classification. The dataset covers European cities distributed in over 34 countries and includes both RGB and multi-spectral versions.
creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth (TU Kaiserslautern and German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI))
citeAs: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth. EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv:1709.00029v2 [cs.CV], 1 Feb 2019.
rai:dataCollection: Satellite images were downloaded from the Sentinel-2A satellite via Amazon S3. Images were selected from European cities covered in the European Urban Atlas, distributed over 34 European countries. Images with low cloud levels were selected. Images were recorded throughout the year to capture high variance in land use and land cover classes. Image patches of 64x64 pixels were extracted and manually checked multiple times, with mislabeled images and images full of snow or ice removed.
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Images with clouds, mislabeling, dead pixels, or ice/snow were identified and discarded. Images with atmospheric effects causing color cast were retained intentionally to allow the classifier to learn these cases.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-spectral satellite images from the Sentinel-2A satellite, downloaded via Amazon S3, covering European cities in the European Urban Atlas across 34 European countries.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Images were extracted from recordings spanning at least from June 2015 (Sentinel-2A launch) onward, recorded throughout the year to capture seasonal variance.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Bands with a lower spatial resolution were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation. RGB images were computed by combining the red (B04), green (B03) and blue (B02) bands. The dataset was released in both RGB and multi-spectral (MS) versions.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Image patches of 64x64 pixels were extracted from satellite images. Images with low cloud coverage were selected using ESA's cloud level value. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times and mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice were removed. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The 10 land use and land cover classes were defined based on visibility at 10 meters per pixel resolution and frequency of coverage in the European Urban Atlas. Class definitions follow the mapping guide of the European Urban Atlas. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times and ground truth was corrected by sorting out mislabeled images.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Images were manually checked multiple times and mislabeled images were removed. Images full of snow or ice were also discarded. Images with atmospheric color cast were retained intentionally.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available at https://github.com/phelber/eurosat. No explicit versioning or deprecation policy is described in the paper.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables applications in agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change monitoring, urban development, and environmental monitoring. It can be used for land use and land cover change detection (e.g., detecting illegal deforestation, urban development) and for assisting in keeping geographical maps up-to-date (e.g., OpenStreetMap).
rai:dataBiases: The dataset distribution is influenced by the number of represented cities per country in the European Urban Atlas. The dataset covers only European cities, which may limit generalizability to other regions. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to European cities covered in the European Urban Atlas. The spatial resolution is 10 meters per pixel, which does not allow identification of fine-grained classes (e.g., churches, schools). The dataset has not received atmospheric correction. A patch-based classification system does not allow finely graduated per-pixel segmentation.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation of deep learning models for land use and land cover classification. Applications include land use and land cover change detection, improvement of geographical maps, urban development monitoring, deforestation detection, and environmental monitoring. The dataset can be used as a benchmark for satellite image classification methods.
